findings.title: Atomic review publication does not preserve or revalidate file permissions
reproduction: Create a valid reviewed fixture, chmod document-reviews.json to 0640, set process umask to 0077, and submit another valid review. docs_review_batch returns RESOLVED but canonical store mode becomes 0600.

Start with canonical store mode 0644 under umask 0022. At the final before_publish recheck boundary, independently chmod the target to 0600 without changing bytes. docs_review_batch returns RESOLVED and replaces it with mode 0644, undoing the permission tightening.
findings.cause: The pending file receives the old mode through os.open, where umask removes bits; fchmod never restores the captured mode. Publication checks only expected content bytes, so a concurrent metadata/permission change is ignored and stale permission bits are restored.
findings.impact: Successful publication can remove access from authorized group readers or undo a concurrent restriction on review metadata. Current budget and publication tests pass under the ambient umask, so they do not prove the stated mode-preservation guarantee.
violated_contract: specs/012-portable-document-lifecycle/contracts/portable-operations.md:41 requires concurrent drift to preserve previous evidence
findings.minimal_fix: Capture and revalidate target identity and permission metadata in addition to expected bytes, reject concurrent drift, and fchmod the pending descriptor to the validated preserved mode before fsync/publication. Keep new-file private defaults and existing byte-budget checks. Add public review-batch tests under a restrictive umask and a deterministic concurrent chmod; update the canonical payload and reseal.
